content.text: Enter Dull, Holofernes, the Pedant and Nathaniel.

lines.text: Very reverend sport, truly, and done in the testimony of a good conscience.
lines.plainText: Very reverend sport truly and done in the testimony of a good conscience

lines.text: The deer was, as you know, sanguis, in blood, ripe as the pomewater, who now hangeth like a jewel in the ear of caelo, the sky, the welkin, the heaven, and anon falleth like a crab on the face of terra, the soil, the land, the earth.
lines.plainText: The deer was as you know sanguis in blood ripe as the pomewater who now hangeth like a jewel in the ear of caelo the sky the welkin the heaven and anon falleth like a crab on the face of terra the soil the land the earth

lines.text: Truly, Master Holofernes, the epithets are sweetly varied, like a scholar at the least. But, sir, I assure ye it was a buck of the first head.
lines.plainText: Truly Master Holofernes the epithets are sweetly varied like a scholar at the least But sir I assure ye it was a buck of the first head

lines.text: Sir Nathaniel, haud credo.
lines.plainText: Sir Nathaniel haud credo

lines.text: 'Twas not a "auld grey doe", 'twas a pricket.
lines.plainText: 'Twas not a auld grey doe 'twas a pricket

lines.text: Most barbarous intimation! Yet a kind of insinuation, as it were, in via, in way, of explication; facere, as it were, replication, or rather, ostentare, to show, as it were, his inclination, after his undressed, unpolished, uneducated, unpruned, untrained, or rather, unlettered, or ratherest, unconfirmed fashion, to insert again my haud credo for a deer.

lines.text: I said the deer was not a "auld grey doe", 'twas a pricket.
lines.plainText: I said the deer was not a auld grey doe 'twas a pricket

lines.text: Twice-sod simplicity, bis coctus!
lines.plainText: Twicesod simplicity bis coctus

lines.text: O, thou monster Ignorance, how deformed dost thou look!
lines.plainText: O thou monster Ignorance how deformed dost thou look

lines.text: Sir, he hath never fed of the dainties that are bred of a book.
lines.plainText: Sir he hath never fed of the dainties that are bred of a book

lines.text: He hath not eat paper, as it were; he hath not drunk ink.
lines.plainText: He hath not eat paper as it were he hath not drunk ink

lines.text: His intellect is not replenished; he is only an animal, only sensible in the duller parts.
lines.plainText: His intellect is not replenished he is only an animal only sensible in the duller parts

lines.text: And such barren plants are set before us that we thankful should be—
lines.plainText: And such barren plants are set before us that we thankful should be

lines.text: Which we of taste and feeling are—for those parts that do fructify in us more than he.
lines.plainText: Which we of taste and feeling arefor those parts that do fructify in us more than he

lines.text: For as it would ill become me to be vain, indiscreet, or a fool,
lines.plainText: For as it would ill become me to be vain indiscreet or a fool

lines.text: So, were there a patch set on learning, to see him in a school.
lines.plainText: So were there a patch set on learning to see him in a school

lines.text: But, omne bene, say I, being of an old father's mind;
lines.plainText: But omne bene say I being of an old father's mind

lines.text: Many can brook the weather that love not the wind.
lines.plainText: Many can brook the weather that love not the wind

lines.text: You two are bookmen. Can you tell me by your wit
lines.plainText: You two are bookmen Can you tell me by your wit

lines.text: What was a month old at Cain's birth, that's not five weeks old as yet?
lines.plainText: What was a month old at Cain's birth that's not five weeks old as yet

lines.text: Dictynna, goodman Dull. Dictynna, goodman Dull.
lines.plainText: Dictynna goodman Dull Dictynna goodman Dull

lines.text: What is Dictynna?
lines.plainText: What is Dictynna

lines.text: A title to Phoebe, to Luna, to the moon.
lines.plainText: A title to Phoebe to Luna to the moon

lines.text: The moon was a month old when Adam was no more,
lines.plainText: The moon was a month old when Adam was no more

lines.text: And raught not to five weeks when he came to five-score.
lines.plainText: And raught not to five weeks when he came to fivescore

lines.text: Th' allusion holds in the exchange.
lines.plainText: Th' allusion holds in the exchange

lines.text: 'Tis true, indeed. The collusion holds in the exchange.
lines.plainText: 'Tis true indeed The collusion holds in the exchange

lines.text: God comfort thy capacity! I say, th' allusion holds in the exchange.
lines.plainText: God comfort thy capacity I say th' allusion holds in the exchange

lines.text: And I say the pollution holds in the exchange, for the moon is never but a month old; and I say beside that 'twas a pricket that the Princess killed.
lines.plainText: And I say the pollution holds in the exchange for the moon is never but a month old and I say beside that 'twas a pricket that the Princess killed

lines.text: Sir Nathaniel, will you hear an extemporal epitaph on the death of the deer? And, to humour the ignorant, call I the deer the Princess killed a pricket.
lines.plainText: Sir Nathaniel will you hear an extemporal epitaph on the death of the deer And to humour the ignorant call I the deer the Princess killed a pricket

lines.text: Perge, good Master Holofernes, perge, so it shall please you to abrogate scurrility.
lines.plainText: Perge good Master Holofernes perge so it shall please you to abrogate scurrility

lines.text: I will something affect the letter; for it argues facility.
lines.plainText: I will something affect the letter for it argues facility

lines.text: The preyful Princess pierced and pricked a pretty pleasing pricket;
lines.plainText: The preyful Princess pierced and pricked a pretty pleasing pricket

lines.text: Some say a sore; but not a sore till now made sore with shooting.
lines.plainText: Some say a sore but not a sore till now made sore with shooting

lines.text: The dogs did yell, put "l" to sore, then sorel jumps from thicket;
lines.plainText: The dogs did yell put l to sore then sorel jumps from thicket

lines.text: Or pricket sore, or else sorel, the people fall a-hooting.
lines.plainText: Or pricket sore or else sorel the people fall ahooting

lines.text: If sore be sore, then "L" to "sore" makes fifty sores o' sorel.
lines.plainText: If sore be sore then L to sore makes fifty sores o' sorel

lines.text: Of one sore I an hundred make, by adding but one more "L".
lines.plainText: Of one sore I an hundred make by adding but one more L

lines.text: A rare talent!
lines.plainText: A rare talent

lines.text: [Aside.] If a talent be a claw, look how he claws him with a talent.
lines.plainText: Aside If a talent be a claw look how he claws him with a talent

lines.text: This is a gift that I have, simple, simple; a foolish extravagant spirit, full of forms, figures, shapes, objects, ideas, apprehensions, motions, revolutions. These are begot in the ventricle of memory, nourished in the womb of pia mater, and delivered upon the mellowing of occasion. But the gift is good in those in whom it is acute, and I am thankful for it.

lines.text: Sir, I praise the Lord for you, and so may my parishioners, for their sons are well tutored by you, and their daughters profit very greatly under you. You are a good member of the commonwealth.
lines.plainText: Sir I praise the Lord for you and so may my parishioners for their sons are well tutored by you and their daughters profit very greatly under you You are a good member of the commonwealth

lines.text: Mehercle! If their sons be ingenious, they shall want no instruction; if their daughters be capable, I will put it to them. But, vir sapit qui pauca loquitur. A soul feminine saluteth us.
lines.plainText: Mehercle If their sons be ingenious they shall want no instruction if their daughters be capable I will put it to them But vir sapit qui pauca loquitur A soul feminine saluteth us

lines.text: God give you good morrow, Master Person.
lines.plainText: God give you good morrow Master Person

lines.text: Master Person, quasi pierce one. And if one should be pierced, which is the one?
lines.plainText: Master Person quasi pierce one And if one should be pierced which is the one

lines.text: Marry, Master schoolmaster, he that is likest to a hogshead.
lines.plainText: Marry Master schoolmaster he that is likest to a hogshead

lines.text: Of piercing a hogshead! A good lustre or conceit in a turf of earth; fire enough for a flint, pearl enough for a swine. 'Tis pretty; it is well.

lines.text: Good Master Parson, be so good as read me this letter. It was given me by Costard, and sent me from Don Armado. I beseech you read it.
lines.plainText: Good Master Parson be so good as read me this letter It was given me by Costard and sent me from Don Armado I beseech you read it

lines.text: and so forth. Ah, good old Mantuan, I may speak of thee as the traveller doth of Venice:

lines.plainText: Ut re sol la mi fa

lines.text: Under pardon, sir, what are the contents? Or rather as Horace says in his—What, my soul, verses?
lines.plainText: Under pardon sir what are the contents Or rather as Horace says in hisWhat my soul verses

lines.text: Ay, sir, and very learned.
lines.plainText: Ay sir and very learned

lines.text: Let me hear a staff, a stanze, a verse,
lines.plainText: Let me hear a staff a stanze a verse

lines.text: If love make me forsworn, how shall I swear to love?
lines.plainText: If love make me forsworn how shall I swear to love

lines.text: Ah, never faith could hold, if not to beauty vowed.
lines.plainText: Ah never faith could hold if not to beauty vowed

lines.text: Though to myself forsworn, to thee I'll faithful prove.
lines.plainText: Though to myself forsworn to thee I'll faithful prove

lines.text: Those thoughts to me were oaks, to thee like osiers bowed.
lines.plainText: Those thoughts to me were oaks to thee like osiers bowed

lines.text: Study his bias leaves, and makes his book thine eyes,
lines.plainText: Study his bias leaves and makes his book thine eyes

lines.text: Where all those pleasures live that art would comprehend.
lines.plainText: Where all those pleasures live that art would comprehend

lines.text: If knowledge be the mark, to know thee shall suffice.
lines.plainText: If knowledge be the mark to know thee shall suffice

lines.text: Well learned is that tongue that well can thee commend,
lines.plainText: Well learned is that tongue that well can thee commend

lines.text: All ignorant that soul that sees thee without wonder;
lines.plainText: All ignorant that soul that sees thee without wonder

lines.text: Which is to me some praise, that I thy parts admire.
lines.plainText: Which is to me some praise that I thy parts admire

lines.text: Thy eye Jove's lightning bears, thy voice his dreadful thunder,
lines.plainText: Thy eye Jove's lightning bears thy voice his dreadful thunder

lines.text: Which, not to anger bent, is music and sweet fire.
lines.plainText: Which not to anger bent is music and sweet fire

lines.text: Celestial as thou art, O, pardon love this wrong,
lines.plainText: Celestial as thou art O pardon love this wrong

lines.text: That sings heaven's praise with such an earthly tongue.

lines.text: You find not the apostrophus, and so miss the accent. Let me supervise the canzonet. [He takes the letter.] Here are only numbers ratified, but, for the elegancy, facility, and golden cadence of poesy, caret. Ovidius Naso was the man. And why indeed "Naso," but for smelling out the odoriferous flowers of fancy, the jerks of invention? Imitari is nothing: so doth the hound his master, the ape his keeper, the tired horse his rider. But, damosella virgin, was this directed to you?

lines.plainText: Ay sir from one Monsieur Berowne one of the strange queen's lords

lines.text: I will overglance the superscript: To the snow-white hand of the most beauteous Lady Rosaline. I will look again on the intellect of the letter, for the nomination of the party writing to the person written unto: Your Ladyship's in all desired employment, Berowne. Sir Nathaniel, this Berowne is one of the votaries with the King, and here he hath framed a letter to a sequent of the stranger queen's, which accidentally, or by the way of progression, hath miscarried. Trip and go, my sweet, deliver this paper into the royal hand of the King. It may concern much. Stay not thy compliment. I forgive thy duty. Adieu.

lines.text: Sir, you have done this in the fear of God, very religiously; and, as a certain Father saith—

lines.text: Sir, tell not me of the Father, I do fear colourable colours. But to return to the verses: did they please you, Sir Nathaniel?

lines.text: Marvellous well for the pen.
lines.plainText: Marvellous well for the pen

lines.text: I do dine today at the father's of a certain pupil of mine, where if, before repast, it shall please you to gratify the table with a grace, I will, on my privilege I have with the parents of the foresaid child or pupil, undertake your ben venuto; where I will prove those verses to be very unlearned, neither savouring of poetry, wit, nor invention. I beseech your society.

lines.text: And certes, the text most infallibly concludes it. [To Dull.] Sir, I do invite you too. You shall not say me nay. Pauca verba. Away! The gentles are at their game, and we will to our recreation.
